requirements.text: creating a new topic category named Engineering Onboarding under the Talent Management COE
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM topic_category WHERE topic_category_id = 13 AND name = 'Engineering Onboarding' AND coe_type = 'Talent Management' AND active = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest topic_category_id in the seed is 12); the only category the task creates
active kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: create an actual case using this new service for our incoming developer Zachary Moore ... Assign it to Global Service Desk, set priority to high, source it as email, COE type Talent Management, and account number ACC-<user_id>-<hr_service_id>

cells.short_description: LIKE 'Product: Engineering New Hire Onboarding, Issue: Technical workstation and access provisioning required%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 55 AND opened_for = 45 AND opened_by = 39 AND short_description LIKE 'Product: Engineering New Hire Onboarding, Issue: Technical workstation and access provisioning required%' AND assignment_group = 3 AND priority = 'high' AND source = 'email' AND coe_type = 'Talent Management' AND account_number = 'ACC-45-55'
requirements.source: Verify HR Case for Zachary Moore using the new service
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id in the seed is 60); the only case the task creates
Zachary Moore is user 45 (the only user of that name) with hr_profile 45; opened_for references hr_profile
opened_by is the requester per policy 3.1: the acting user Karen Watkins, hr_profile 39
the description is the request's text; a trailing full stop is allowed since the request's sentence ends there
Global Service Desk is user_group 3, the only group of that name
account number from user_id 45 and the new hr_service_id 55; his hr_profile id is also 45, so the benchmark's opened_for-based form agrees

disagreement: opened_by: A 39, B untested; chose 39 because policy 3.1 defines opened_by as the requester, here the acting user Karen Watkins (hr_profile 39), who asks for the case for 'our incoming developer'

notes:
disagreement: value: the case's opened_by: one pass tests 39, the other leaves it untested; kept 39 because policy 3.1 makes opened_by the requester, the acting user (logged in the requirement).
disagreement: form: the active cells on the category, detail, template and service: one pass writes 1, the other true; the two are equal in SQLite, and 1 is kept because the seed stores active as the integer 1.
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition (all five checks kept); their texts and assumptions differ in wording only.
No listed tool updates a service after creation, so the service can carry the template link only if the template is created first, although the request names the template after the service.
The case check builds the account number from opened_for (an hr_profile id) whereas the request says user_id; for Zachary Moore both are 45, so the requirement fixes ACC-45-55.
The request's own 'Product: , Issue: ' description takes precedence over the policy's 'Service: , Subject: , Detail: ' template.
The case's status is not tested: the request does not state one and the policy's default state 'new' is not a status this database uses.
The acting user Karen Watkins holds the admin role: the policy lets administrators create HR services and manage system tables, which covers the category, detail and template, but says they must not perform routine HR case work; the request and the benchmark's checks expect the case, so the requirement follows them.
